title: Emergency patch and observation runbook for guided retries during 5xx waves
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported recurring 5xx spikes and elevated latency in hosted endpoints between 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC and 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC. Symptoms: a) transient 502/504 bursts, b) amplified retry loops from SDKs causing secondary overload, c) elevated connection churn and partial KV cache misses. Impact: customer-facing APIs degraded for several tenants (multi-tenant surface), several escalations to SE/CS teams. Goal: ship a narrow emergency patch to stop retry amplification and stabilize request paths, and produce an operational runbook for guided retries and fast mitigation during escalations.
investigation_summary: Initial telemetry showed two correlated signals: increased upstream model request latency in us-east-1 and a spike in client-side retries from a small subset of high-traffic tenants. Connection pool exhaustion on inference proxies combined with circuit-breaker timeouts that were too long led to threads queuing and additional client retries. We observed KV cache eviction rates spike (prefix misses) and a model variant rotation that increased memory pressure on a subset of nodes. No single code regression was identified; the failure mode is emergent from config + load pattern during tenant surges.
root_cause_hypothesis: Retry amplification: SDKs continued aggressive retries while backend latency transiently increased, causing feedback loop.
Proxy connection pool saturation: default pool sizes and long connection timeouts allowed queued requests to accumulate and trigger 5xx responses under surge.
KV cache miss storm: model variant change increased cache churn leading to additional downstream compute and longer tail latencies.
mitigation_deployed: 2026-03-10 01:15 UTC: Temporarily reduced SDK client default retry window via feature flag (sdk-guided-retries=false) for affected tenants.
2026-03-10 02:00 UTC: Decreased proxy connection keepalive timeout from 90s -> 20s for canary pool to release sockets faster.
2026-03-10 02:30 UTC: Tightened circuit-breaker thresholds for model backend calls (failures tripped at 2 failures/10s) to fail fast instead of queuing.
2026-03-10 03:10 UTC: Deployed targeted autoscale increase for GPU serving pool in us-east-1 (burst nodes) to lower tail latency while longer-term fix is prepared.
planned_work: Implement server-side guided retry header support: honor X-Redwood-Client-Retry-Policy and return Retry-After when backpressure is appropriate.
Add per-tenant adaptive max inflight requests and queue limits to prevent a single tenant from exhausting proxy resources.
Introduce an emergency rollback knob for model variant rotations at the router level and automated pinning when tail latency crosses threshold.
Ship conservative SDK default changes in a minor release (reduce retry backoff aggressiveness + jitter) and coordinate with partner SEs for client upgrades.
Create a dedicated dashboard and SLO alert for retry amplification (retries per 1k requests and retry-to-success ratio) and add to escalation pager rotations.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate tenant surge: replay production trace of tenant X at 3x normal request rate against a canary pool with tight connection limits.
Introduce artificial backend latency (sleep 300-700ms) on model-serving instances and observe proxy queue length and 5xx emissions.
Run a small workload with legacy SDK retry settings to validate amplification and measure RPS and retry counts via canary tracing.
Toggle sdk-guided-retries flag and rerun to confirm reduction in client-side retry loop and stabilization of queues.
acceptance_criteria: No sustained 5xx burst periods (>2% error rate) in canary for 48h under replayed surge traffic.
Retry amplification metric reduced by >=75% in canary (baseline to post-patch) for same workload.
Per-tenant priority and inflight limits prevent any single tenant from exceeding 60% of proxy connection pool capacity.
Runbook validated by on-call SRE and documented in Confluence with step-by-step mitigation and rollback instructions.
review_feedback_and_decisions: PM (Jesse Wu): prioritize guided-retry header and runbook over SDK breaking defaults — minimal customer impact path preferred.
SRE (Maria Gomez): recommended tightening CBs and short-term keepalive reduction; warned about risk of aggressive timeouts causing premature disconnects.
Engineering (Igor Novak): proposed an incremental approach: canary guided-retry + metric flags -> broader rollout after 48h steady state.
Design for telemetry (Lina Park): requested better per-tenant drilldowns and tagging to separate noisy tenants from platform regressions.
next_steps: Complete server-side guided-retry implementation and merge PR #6123 (owner: Marco Li).
Coordinate SDK release plan with SDK team (owner: Priya Shah) and notify top-10 customers for early upgrade window.
Add canary alarms and smoke tests to CI that inject controlled backend latency to validate circuit-breaker behavior.
Schedule postmortem meeting and assign action owners for long-term hardening (KV cache eviction tuning, model variant rollout policy).
postmortem_todo: Perform root-cause analysis on KV cache churn and correlate with model variant rotations (owner: Research/Applied ML).
Evaluate connection pool sizing logic and consider dynamic pool resizing based on observed per-tenant concurrency patterns.
Document SLA impact to affected customers and prepare targeted communications with CS (owner: Customer Success).
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive server-side timeouts reduce queueing but increase chance of client reconnects—we prefer controlled fail-fast behavior and explicit Retry-After guidance.
We will avoid large sweeping SDK changes without coordinated customer outreach; the server-side guided-retry header gives immediate control to the platform.
